recentItems.title: "Greater Columbus": Up Close with Malcolm Cochran
recentItems.description:
Thursday, May 28, 6:00–7:00 PM
Columbus Museum of Art

This program offers a rare opportunity to hear directly from local artist Malcolm Cochran about his work in "Greater Columbus: The 2026 Visual Arts Fellowship Exhibition." In dialogue with Rae Root, CMA’s Roy Lichtenstein Curatorial Fellow and curator of "Greater Columbus," Cochran will reflect on his practice, process, and ideas.

This program is free for members, $5 for nonmembers.

ABOUT MALCOLM COCHRAN
Malcolm Cochran works across mediums on large-scale sculptures, installations, and public art with an emphasis on place and implicit human presence and histories. He has exhibited at Artpark, MoMA PS1, Socrates Sculpture Park, the Wexner Center, Columbus Museum of Art, Contemporary Art Center, Weston Art Gallery, Cleveland Center for Contemporary Art, Eastern State Penitentiary, Retretti Art Center, Finland, and Het Stroomhuis, Holland. Permanent public commissions include Brattleboro VT, Cleveland, Columbus, and Dublin OH, and Hudson River Park, NYC. He is the recipient of awards from the National Endowment for the Arts, the Bellagio Center Residency Award, Italy, Awards in the Visual Arts 9, the OAC and GCAC, and a Cité Internationale des Arts residency, Paris. His "Goodale Park Fountain" received an Americans for the Arts 2014 Public Art Network Year in Review Award. In 2017 he was named the International Sculpture Center Educator of the Year. From 1987–2013, he was on the sculpture faculty at The Ohio State University.

recentItems.title: Sadie Barnette on "The New Eagle Creek Saloon"
recentItems.description:
Tuesday, April 7, 6:00–7:00 PM
Columbus Museum of Art at The Pizzuti

Join us for a special talk by Oakland-based artist Sadie Barnette, who will discuss her project "The New Eagle Creek Saloon" (2019–ongoing). Honoring the legacy of the Eagle Creek Saloon, the first Black-owned gay bar in San Francisco, which her father founded in the early 1990s, Barnette reanimates the bar as a communal hub and gathering place, celebrating its resistant, joyous spirit. 

This program is free with registration. "Bar Room" will be open for event patrons to enjoy from 5:00–8:00 PM.

This program is presented with generous support from The Ohio State University Office of Academic Affairs.

ABOUT SADIE BARNETTE
Sadie Barnette is an artist working in a wide variety of visual outputs, often all at once. She was born and raised in Oakland, California and holds a BFA from CalArts and an MFA from UC San Diego. Her work has been equally influenced by the history of conceptual art, Bay Area rappers, anxiety, car culture, and Hello Kitty. Barnette’s work has recently been featured in exhibitions at the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York; Walker Art Center, Minneapolis; San Francisco Museum of Modern Art; Institute of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles; The Studio Museum in Harlem, and Museum of Contemporary Art Denver, among many others. She has been awarded grants and residencies including the Studio Museum in Harlem, United States Artists Fellowship, UC Berkeley’s Black Studies Collaboratory, and is a 2026 Creative Capital fellow. She lives in Oakland, CA.

recentItems.title: Leslie King-Hammond and Lowery Stokes Sims in conversation with Sampada Aranke and Allie Tepper
recentItems.description:
Saturday, January 10, 4:00–5:30 PM
Columbus Museum of Art at The Pizzuti

On the last weekend of "Las Vegas Ikebana: Maren Hassinger and Senga Nengudi," legendary curators and art historians Leslie King-Hammond and Lowery Stokes Sims were joined by Ohio State professor Sampada Aranke and guest curator Allie Tepper for a conversation on friendship, collaboration, and the community that supported Hassinger and Nengudi over the decades.

This program was free with registration. This program is supported by the Franklin County Board of Commissioners.

recentItems.title: Gregory Buchakjian in conversation on Artemisia Gentileschi's "Hercules and Omphale"
recentItems.description:
Wednesday, May 27, 11:00 AM–12:00 PM

In the aftermath of the 2020 Beirut port explosion, Lebanese artist and art historian Gregory Buchakjian led efforts to rescue and restore Artemisia Gentileschi’s painting "Hercules and Omphale," which had been severely damaged in the blast. Thanks to his advocacy, the painting has now been restored by the Getty Museum in Los Angeles and is currently on view at CMA alongside a new photographic installation by Buchakjian. In this virtual conversation with Curator of Collections and Exhibitions Daniel Marcus, Buchakjian will discuss his long history with the painting, which he discovered as a student in the 1990s, and its ongoing significance to the city of Beirut.

recentItems.title: Freedom Sounds: Tavares Strachan and Hanif Abdurraqib in Conversation at The Pizzuti
recentItems.description:
On Friday, October 24, 2025, alongside the public unveiling of Tavares Strachan’s permanent installation "Bar Room," we hosted a landmark conversation between Strachan and Hanif Abdurraqib, both of whom are MacArthur Fellows.

This event brought together two visionary artists whose work explores the rootedness of history and identity in spaces of communal belonging. Strachan, a Bahamian-born, New York-based conceptual artist, and Abdurraqib, a Columbus native and critically acclaimed poet, essayist, and cultural critic, discussed the places and communities that have empowered their creative work.

Moderated by CMA curator Daniel Marcus, their dialogue sets the stage for "Tavares Strachan: The Day Tomorrow Began," a major exhibition of Strachan’s work opening at The Pizzuti on May 16, 2026.

This program was supported by the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

recentItems.title: In Conversation: Tacita Dean and Ann Hamilton
recentItems.description: Tacita Dean: Blind Folly is the first major museum survey in the United States of work by British European artist Tacita Dean (b. 1965). Organized in close collaboration with the artist, the exhibition highlights her singular approach to drawing, film, and printmaking—embracing chance, intuition, and material process. The show features monumental blackboard drawings alongside rarely-seen works on paper, found postcard works, early photographs, and 16mm films.
